title: A core's own Part History page shows its name and its own history
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test with a Core Charge of $25.00, so it has a core, then change part A's description once in its Edit Inventory Part window, from description 1 to description 2.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Open the core's own Part History page.
  2. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  3. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  4. Click the clock icon (Part History) at the left of the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A Part History page opens for the core, not for part A.
  • Its Part details panel names the core "Core for" followed by description 2: the core was renamed with its part.
  • Its newest entry reads "Description updated | Original description: Core for" description 1 "| New description: Core for" description 2, with your name under Staff and today's date and time.

Step 2:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 3:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 4:

  • Part A's own newest entry reads "Description updated | Original description:" description 1 "| New description:" description 2: the core keeps a history of its own.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • S13-R15: “A changed description also renames the part's core, which reads "Core for {description}".”
  • S10-R24: “A changed description writes "Description updated | Original description: {old} | New description: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.”
  • S10-R26: “When the part has a core, the core gets the same number or description entry. The core's description entries read its own description, "Core for {description}".”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
